symptom_text: Angular leaf spot of bean produces angular, water-soaked lesions on leaves that are sharply delimited by leaf veins, giving them a distinctly geometric, polygonal shape. As lesions mature they turn brown to reddish-brown or gray-brown with a darker brown border, and the centers may dry out and fall away leaving ragged holes. On the undersides of leaves a grayish-white to silvery sporulation (conidia) of the fungus is often visible. Lesions can also appear on pods as reddish-brown, circular to irregular spots, and on stems as elongated, dark brown streaks. Severe infections cause premature defoliation and significant yield loss.

pathogen.verbatim_quote: Pseudocercospora griseola (Sacc.) Crous & U. Braun (formerly known as Phaeoisariopsis griseola) is the causal agent of angular leaf spot of bean.

affected_organs.verbatim_quote: Symptoms occur on leaves, pods and stems of susceptible bean cultivars.

visual_symptoms.value: Angular, water-soaked lesions delimited by leaf veins turning brown to gray-brown; grayish sporulation on leaf undersides; reddish-brown spots on pods; dark streaks on stems
visual_symptoms.verbatim_quote: On leaves, lesions are angular, delimited by veins, initially water-soaked, later turning brown to grey-brown, with a darker border; on the lower leaf surface a grey, powdery sporulation is visible; on pods, lesions are circular to irregular, reddish-brown spots.

symptom_text: Common bacterial blight of beans, caused by Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. phaseoli, produces water-soaked, irregularly shaped lesions on leaves that rapidly enlarge and turn brown and necrotic, often surrounded by a distinctive bright yellow halo. These lesions may coalesce to cover large areas of the leaf blade, causing extensive blighting. On pods, water-soaked spots develop and turn reddish-brown, sometimes with a creamy bacterial exudate visible on the surface. Infected seeds may show yellow or wrinkled discoloration. Symptoms are distributed across leaves, pods, and seeds, and are most severe under warm, humid conditions.

pathogen.value: Xanthomonas campestris (axonopodis) pv. phaseoli; Xanthomonas fuscans subsp. fuscans

affected_organs.value: Leaf margins and interveinal areas; whole leaves in severe cases
affected_organs.verbatim_quote: The spots or lesions develop on the edges or interveinal areas of leaves.

visual_symptoms.value: Water-soaked or light green spots enlarging to brown necrotic centres, bordered by a diagnostic lemon-yellow ring
visual_symptoms.verbatim_quote: These irregularly shaped spots are bordered by a lemon yellow ring, which serves as a diagnostic symptom of common bacterial blight.

symptom_text: Halo blight of bean, caused by Pseudomonas savastanoi pv. phaseolicola, primarily affects leaves, pods, and seeds. On leaves, small water-soaked spots first appear, which enlarge and turn brown to reddish-brown necrotic lesions surrounded by a conspicuous wide, pale green to yellow chlorotic halo — the hallmark symptom giving the disease its name. Lesions are angular to irregular in shape, often delimited by leaf veins, and may coalesce under wet conditions to cause extensive blighting. On pods, water-soaked, greasy-looking spots develop and may become reddish-brown with age. Seeds from infected pods may show a wrinkled, discolored appearance. Symptoms are most severe under cool, wet weather conditions and can be distributed across the entire canopy when the pathogen is seed-borne.

affected_organs.value: Leaves (undersurfaces first), extending to upper plant parts
affected_organs.verbatim_quote: small, angular, water-soaked spots (almost resembling little pin pricks) on the undersurfaces of leaves

visual_symptoms.value: Angular water-soaked spots with a light green to yellow halo; general chlorosis of leaves and upper plant in severe cases
visual_symptoms.verbatim_quote: a characteristic light green to yellow halo appears around the spots

symptom_text: Bean common mosaic virus causes distinctive foliar symptoms characterized by irregular light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves, creating a mottled appearance across the leaf surface. Affected leaves often display puckering, downward curling, and malformation with a blistered or crinkled texture. The mosaic pattern consists of alternating patches of normal green tissue interspersed with chlorotic yellow-green areas, giving leaves an uneven coloration. Trifoliate leaves may become narrowed, elongated, and distorted. Plants infected early show stunting and reduced vigor, with symptoms most pronounced on younger developing leaves. In severe cases, leaves may exhibit vein banding where darker green tissue follows along the veins while interveinal areas remain lighter.

visual_symptoms.value: Light green-yellow and dark green mosaic on trifoliolate leaves with puckering, blistering, distortion and downward curling
visual_symptoms.verbatim_quote: mosaic patterns of light green-yellow leaf tissue, dark green tissue, or both light and dark mosaics together on the trifoliolate leaves. Leaf discoloration is usually accompanied by puckering, blistering, distortion, and a downward curling and rolling.

symptom_text: Bean rust, caused by Uromyces appendiculatus, primarily affects leaves but can also infect stems and pods. On the upper leaf surface, small pale yellow or white spots first appear, while the corresponding lower leaf surface develops raised, brick-red to reddish-brown powdery pustules (uredinia) that are circular and approximately 1–2 mm in diameter. These pustules rupture the epidermis and release masses of reddish-brown urediniospores, giving infected tissue a rusty, powdery appearance. As the disease progresses, pustules may coalesce, and surrounding tissue often turns yellow and necrotic. Later in the season, darker brown to black teliospore pustules (telia) may form on the same or adjacent lesions. Severely infected leaves may drop prematurely, and heavily infected pods show similar reddish-brown pustules on their surface.

affected_organs.value: Leaves, primarily the lower surface; pods may also be affected

visual_symptoms.value: Dry reddish, yellowish or orange powdery spore pustules, mainly on the underside of leaves
visual_symptoms.verbatim_quote: Plants infected with rust have dry reddish, yellowish, or orange spore masses or pustules primarily on the lower surface of leaves.
